To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the reactions of heteryllanes with nucleophilic agents are characterized by sequential substitution of the nucleophilic heterocyclic group.

nucleophilic substitution reactions of heterysilanes and heterylgermanes are characterized by the formation of the corresponding heteroorganometallic compounds, which are then converted to the corresponding heterylmetals by the action of nucleophiles.

the reactions of furylsilanes and furylgermanes with nucleophilic O-, N-, S-, and C- reagents are complicated by the formation of 2,5-dioxofuran derivatives, whereas the reactions of dihydrofurylsilanes and dihydrofurylermanes with nucleophiles are characterized by a high degree of regioselectivity and the formation of the corresponding mono- and disubstituted dihydrofurylderivatives.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the synthesis and reactivity of heterosilicon and heterogermanium compounds, which are of interest for the development of new synthetic methods and for the creation of new organosilicon and organogermanium materials.
the synthesis of new heterylsilane derivatives and their use in organic synthesis.

reactions of heteryldichlorosilanes and heteryldichlo-germanes in nucleophilic substitutions, reactions of heterylhydrosilicones in the formation of heterylalkoxysilanes and heteroylsiloxanes, and reactions of heterylmethylchlorosilanes and -chlorogermanes with Grignard reagents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

in nucleophilic reactions of furyl-, pyranyl-, and tetraheterocyclic silanes and germanes, the nucleophile attacks the silicon atom, and the nucleophilic heterocyclic group is substituted for the hydrosilane or hydrosiliconium ion.
the reactions of heterosilicon compounds with nucleophilic agents are determined by the nature of the substituent on the silicon atom and by the nature of nucleophile.

the reactions of heterylhydrosilane and -hydrosilicones with nucleophilic substances are not only the basis of the synthesis of heteroorganosilanes and -organosilicons, but also the source of the synthesis of new heterocyclic compounds.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nucleophilic reactivity of the heterocyclic groups in heterylsilane and heterylsiloxane derivatives is higher than the corresponding reactivity of heteroaromatics.
the reactivity of the heterosilanes is determined not only by the structure of the heterocycle, but also by the nature of the substituents at the heteroatom.
the reactivity of the Si-H bond in the heterosilanes is determined mainly by the structure of the heterocyclic substituent.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the reactivity of the heterocyclic group in the heterylhydrosilane or -hydrosiliconium ion is determined by the nature of the nucleophilic reagent and the nature of the group bonded to the heterocycle.
the reactivity of heterylsilanols, heterylsiloxanes, heterylsilyl halides, and heterylsilylamines is determined by the nature of the heterocycle.

the reactivity of heterylsilanols and heterylsiloxanes is higher than that of heterylsilyl ethers, and that the reactivity decreases in the series: furyl > dihydrofuryls > tetrahydrofurryl > dihydropyranyll > tetrahydropyranyl.
